title: Existence of normalized finite Tate balancing and source compatibilities
statement: Let φ : A → B be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by a positive integer N, and let X be a scheme on which N is invertible. For the actual scalar/single, shift, tensor and pullback comparisons and predicates in [def-pur-finite-tate-scalar-source-data], there exists a family β_r : Q_X(A_X(r)) ≅ B_X(r) satisfying the generator, degree-zero and tensor-power balancing equations, the single/unit and shifted-line normalization, invertibility of every unbounded source map, and the coefficient-unit and zero-power source equations. This assertion does not include uniqueness of β or the flat-single comparison for arbitrary flat sheaves.

proof.text: For $M=A_T$, compose the comparison just computed with $A_T\otimes_A A'_T\to A'_T$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\varphi(a)b$. Its inverse sends $b$ to $1\otimes b$: the two composites are the identity by the balancing relation $a\otimes b=1\otimes\varphi(a)b$. The scalar adjunction unit sends $a$ to $a\otimes1$, so the composite sends it to $\varphi(a)$. This identifies the composite with the specified normalized coefficient-unit map $u_T$, with no unspecified unit automorphism.

By [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], every $A_T(r)$ is flat. Define the ordinary line balancing map $\beta_1:(A_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}\mu_{N,T})\otimes_A A'_T\to A'_T\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}\mu_{N,T}$ by $(a\otimes z)\otimes b\mapsto\varphi(a)b\otimes z$. It is balanced over both rings; its inverse is $b\otimes z\mapsto(1\otimes z)\otimes b$, and the balancing relation verifies both composites on pure tensors. These sectionwise formulas commute with restrictions and therefore induce inverse maps after sheafification. For $r>1$ the identical construction on $r$ root-of-unity factors sends $(\bigotimes_i(a_i\otimes z_i))\otimes b$ to $b\prod_i\varphi(a_i)\otimes(\bigotimes_i z_i)$, using the canonical regrouping of the tensor powers. Its inverse inserts $1$ in each $A$ factor. At $r=0$ use multiplication from Step 3. Thus $q_{A_T(r)}$ followed by $\beta_r$ is the required unshifted line isomorphism.

The scalar tensorator is the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for the identity topos with ring map $A_T\to A'_T$. On flat K-flat representatives it is the ordinary balancing isomorphism $((x\otimes y)\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes b)$; its inverse multiplies the two $A'$ coefficients. Consequently the $r$-factor formula in Step 4 is precisely the tensor power of the rank-one formula, with these specified tensorators. Applying termwise scalar extension to a shifted complex commutes with the shift: both have terms $P^{i+n}\otimes_A A'$ and differential $(-1)^n(d_P\otimes1)$. Localizing this equality gives the specified scalar/shift comparison. Shift the line map by $2r$ to obtain $l_{T,r}$. At $r=0$ this is Step 3; all rearrangements of line factors here have even degree and introduce sign $+1$.

proof.text:
Put $L=A_X(r)[2r]$. The specified map is the following composite:
$$Q_X(f^*K\otimes_A^L L)\xrightarrow{\mu}Q_X(f^*K)\otimes_{A'}^LQ_XL\xrightarrow{\lambda^{-1}\otimes l_{X,r}}f^*(Q_YK)\otimes_{A'}^LA'_X(r)[2r].$$
Here $\mu$ is the ringed-topos tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and $\lambda:f^*Q_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_Xf^*$ is the canonical scalar/pullback identification specified before the bounded-below mate assertion in [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection]. That identification concerns all ordinary unbounded derived inputs; none of the later hypotheses on its mate $J$ are being used. Each arrow is an isomorphism, so their composite gives $a_{f,K}$ for every $K$, without flatness of $A'$ over $A$.

proof.text: Check the claimed boundary normalizations on representatives, not by choosing new isomorphisms. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ for $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; pullback preserves this class by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The scalar/pullback identification is ordinary coefficient balancing on $f^*P$, with the scalar insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, as specified in [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection]. For $K=A_Y[0]$ the tensorator sends $(a\otimes v)\otimes b$ to $(a\otimes1)\otimes(v\otimes b)$. Multiplication on the first factor and $\beta_r$ on the second send this to $\beta_r((av)\otimes b)$, exactly the line comparison of Steps 3--5. For $r=0$ and general homogeneous $x\in f^*P$, the same calculation sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes\varphi(a)b$, whose right unitor is $x\otimes\varphi(a)b$. Applying the source unitor first gives this same element under scalar/pullback. These are balanced sheaf maps and chain maps in each degree; hence their localized maps are equal. This proves both normalizations for the actual comparisons, including unbounded $K$. Alternatively transport the tensor and pullback unit equations in lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence, and use the scalar right-unit equation at zero power.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_tate_scalar_source_normalization_exists [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (hA : (N : A) = 0) (hB : (N : B) = 0)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (N : X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ β : ∀ r : ℕ,
        (Etale.purityScalarSheaf φ X).obj (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateTwist X N A hA r) ≅
          Scheme.finiteEtaleTateTwist X N B hB r,
      IsFiniteTateScalarBalancing φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarLineNormalized φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceInvertible φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceUnitNormalized φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceZeroNormalized φ N hA hB X β
